questions.q: Which dog did Francois first put in the lead after Spitz was gone?
choices: Dave, the experienced wheel-dog at the back
Sol-leks, whom he judged the best lead-dog left
Billee, the most good-natured dog in the whole team
Pike, the clever dog who pulled just behind Buck
questions.evidence: In his judgment, Sol-leks was the best lead-dog left.

questions.q: Why did Buck keep away from the men and refuse to go to his old place in the team?
choices: He was afraid that Francois was going to give him a thrashing
He was too badly hurt from the fight to pull the sled that day
He wanted to run off into the woods and live with the wolves
He wanted the leadership, which he felt he had earned
questions.evidence: He wanted, not to escape a clubbing, but to have the leadership.

questions.q: Why did Buck back away when Francois came at him with a heavy club?
choices: He remembered the man in the red sweater
He knew that Perrault would punish him later
He was too weak to fight after losing blood
He wanted Sol-leks to fight the man instead
questions.evidence: Buck remembered the man in the red sweater

questions.q: What finally made Buck trot in and take his place at the head of the team?
choices: Francois offered him a large piece of frozen fish
Perrault tied a rope to his collar and pulled him in
Francois threw down the club as Perrault told him to
Sol-leks walked away and left the lead place empty
questions.evidence: Francois complied, whereupon Buck trotted in

questions.q: "Francois was obdurate" when he kept putting Sol-leks back in the lead. What does "obdurate" mean?
choices: Stubborn and unwilling to change
Kind and gentle with the dogs
Confused about what to do next
Tired after a long night awake
questions.evidence: Francois was obdurate

questions.q: How good was Buck as a leader, compared to Spitz?
choices: He was much slower, and the team often got lost
He was even better than Spitz at quick thinking
He was about the same, but the dogs liked him a little more
He was worse at first, but slowly learned how to lead
questions.evidence: he showed himself the superior even of Spitz

questions.q: Why didn't Dave and Sol-leks mind that Buck was the new leader?
choices: They had always disliked Spitz and were glad that he was gone
They were afraid Buck would punish them if they ever complained
They only cared about toiling hard in the traces
They were too old and tired to notice who led the team
questions.evidence: Their business was to toil, and toil mightily, in the traces.

questions.q: How did Pike change after Buck became leader?
choices: He pulled harder than ever
He began to hide in the snow every morning
He tried to take the lead place from Buck
He stopped stealing food from the other dogs
questions.evidence: he was pulling more than ever before in his life

questions.q: Which two native huskies joined the team at the Rink Rapids?
choices: Billee and Joe
Dub and Dolly
Pike and Sol-leks
Teek and Koona
questions.evidence: two native huskies, Teek and Koona, were added

questions.q: Why was the trip back to Skaguay called a record run?
choices: They had carried more gold than any team before them
They averaged forty miles a day for fourteen days
They lost no dogs at all on the whole of the trip
They crossed every river without breaking through
questions.evidence: Each day for fourteen days they had averaged forty miles.

questions.q: What happened when official orders came for Perrault and Francois at Skaguay?
choices: They harnessed Buck and started back to Dawson with the mail
They sold the whole team to a gold miner for a thousand dollars
Francois hugged Buck and wept, and they left Buck's life for good
They took Buck aboard a ship heading back to Seattle
questions.evidence: Francois called Buck to him, threw his arms around him, wept over him.

questions.q: What was Buck's new team carrying on the trail back to Dawson?
choices: Mail for the men who were looking for gold
Gold dust from the mines down to the coast
Food and tools for a new police camp
Logs and firewood for the miners' cabins
questions.evidence: for this was the mail train

questions.q: "It was a monotonous life, operating with machine-like regularity. One day was very like another." What does "monotonous" mean?
choices: Exciting and full of danger
The same over and over, dull
Lonely and far from others
Short and quickly over
questions.evidence: One day was very like another.

questions.q: When Buck lay by the fire and thought of Judge Miller's place, how did he feel?
choices: He was terribly homesick and longed to go back
He was not homesick at all
He was angry at the Judge for letting Manuel take him
He was confused and could no longer remember the house
questions.evidence: He was not homesick.

questions.q: Who was the short, hairy man Buck seemed to see by "another fire"?
choices: A man from long ago, like those his wild ancestors had known
The half-breed cook, seen through the smoke of the fire
A miner who had lost his way in the snow and found their camp
Manuel, the gardener's helper, in one of Buck's bad dreams
questions.evidence: the memories of his heredity

questions.q: How did the drivers on the mail train take care of their dogs each night?
choices: They let the tired dogs sleep inside the warm tents right beside them
They fed the dogs first and checked their feet before sleeping
They gave the dogs a full day of rest every third day
They rubbed the dogs with oil to keep away the frost
questions.evidence: They ate before the drivers ate

questions.q: Which dog suffered the most on the hard trip back from Dawson?
choices: Billee, who cried in his sleep
Joe, who grew sourer than ever
Dave, who had something wrong inside
Sol-leks, who was blind in one eye
questions.evidence: But it was Dave who suffered most of all.

questions.q: What did Dave do after the driver took him out of the team and put Sol-leks in his place?
choices: He ran quietly behind the sled where the trail was easy
He lay down in the snow and refused to move all day
He bit through Sol-leks's traces and stood in his old place
He ran off alone into the woods by the river and was never seen again
questions.evidence: Dave had bitten through both of Sol-leks's traces

questions.q: Why did the drivers decide to put the sick Dave back in the harness?
choices: They needed every dog to pull the heavy load of mail
They thought that the hard work in harness might make him well again
They believed a dog could break its heart if kept from its work
They wanted him to rest by riding on top of the sled
questions.evidence: a dog could break its heart through being denied the work that killed it

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Buck winning the lead and the pride sled dogs take in their work
Buck trying to escape so that he can find his way back home
Perrault and Francois searching up and down the trail for the missing Spitz
The miners of Skaguay fighting over who will own Buck's team
questions.evidence: the pride of trace and trail was his
